text: dsh-run-speed 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的会话级并行策略插件。它在输入栏提供运行速度菜单，也注册 /run-speed 命令，支持 Standard、Fast、Turbo 三种模式。Fast 与 Turbo 会向系统提示加入并行工作指导，建议最多并行启动 3 个或在适用时启动 4 至 6 个子 agent，同时保留当前 provider、模型和 reasoning effort，并要求依赖任务串行处理。模式按会话保存在 Host 进程内，重启后恢复 Standard。适合希望分别调整各会话并行程度的 DSH 用户；代码没有读取密钥或配置外部服务。

dsh-run-speed adds per-session parallel controls to DSH through a composer menu and /run-speed command. Fast and Turbo add guidance for parallel subagents while preserving the selected model. Modes reset after restart; no API key or external service is configured.
想给不同 DSH 会话分别设置并行处理强度。
我想让 DSH 在不切换模型或推理强度的情况下并行处理独立任务。
Can I choose a faster parallel-work policy for one session without changing its model?
dsh-run-speed 的功能「会话运行速度选择」：从输入栏菜单或 /run-speed 命令选择 Standard、Fast、Turbo，为当前会话添加对应的并行子 agent 指导。
dsh-run-speed 的维护与更新元数据：活跃维护；距最后推送 36 天；提交数 2；更新频次 unknown；近 90 天提交 未知；开放 Issue 未知；仓库健康分 62/100（置信度 low）。

description: "A per-session run-speed selector for DSH that adds parallel-execution guidance without changing the selected model or reasoning effort."

dsh-run-speed README · dsh-run-speed：This optional DSH bundle adds a **Run speed** menu to the composer and a matching `/run-speed` command. It lets you
choose, per session, how aggressively the agent may fan work out to parallel background subagents while the selected
provider, model, and reasoning effort stay exactly as they are.

dsh-run-speed README · dsh-run-speed：| Mode | Added prompt text | Parallel subagents | 中文 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Standard | none | the model's normal strategy | 标准 |
| Fast | one dynamic prompt section | up to 3, launched together in one message | 快速 |
| Turbo | one dynamic prompt section | 4 through 6 | 极速 |

dsh-run-speed README · dsh-run-speed：The plugin never switches provider, model, or reasoning effort, and it never patches Harness core packages. Install or
remove the bundle through the DSH plugin manager; `cordis.patch.yml` contributes a single plugin entry
(`id: run-speed`).

Repository: <https://github.com/yjc925925/dsh-run-speed>

dsh-run-speed README · Usage：The composer control and the command are two views of the same state: the button drives the Host command through the
remote command service, reads the authoritative mode back from it when it mounts, and adopts the mode it just applied
after a switch succeeds. Both the English words and the Chinese equivalents are accepted; bare `/run-speed` and
`/run-speed status` report the current mode.

dsh-run-speed README · Usage：```
/run-speed                 # -> "Run speed: standard."
/run-speed fast            # -> "Run speed set to fast. Model and reasoning effort remain unchanged."
/run-speed 极速            # same as /run-speed turbo
```

The composer control sits in the `conversation.input.right` slot (order `30`) and is disabled while the session is
running or removed, and while a switch is in flight.

dsh-run-speed README · What the model sees：Fast and Turbo contribute one dynamic system-prompt section (`user:run-speed`, order `425`). Its text tells the parent
and every child to keep the current provider, model, and reasoning effort, to batch independent parallel-safe tool
calls, to keep dependent work serial rather than delegating it, and to partition file ownership so that two agents
never write the same file. Standard contributes an empty section — the section itself is always registered, but its
text is an empty string, so no tokens are spent.

dsh-run-speed README · Token effect：Fast and Turbo add a short fixed prompt and can spend substantially more tokens overall by running parallel
subagents. Standard adds no model tokens.

dsh-run-speed README · KV Cache effect：Changing modes replaces the active system prompt on the next model request and can start a new reusable request
prefix. Flipping modes back and forth therefore costs cache re-use on the following request.

dsh-run-speed README · Layout：The repository ships the prebuilt `lib/` artifacts, so the bundle can be installed and run without a build step. The
sources are published alongside them for review and for future maintenance.

dsh-run-speed README · Development：This package is developed as a member of the `deepseek-harness` monorepo at `packages/client/ui-run-speed/`. Committed
here are the sources, the Vitest suite, and the build configuration, because the npm tarball's `files` allowlist
excluded all of them.

dsh-run-speed README · Development：**A standalone build is not wired up yet.** The build and type-check configuration reaches into monorepo scaffolding
that this repository does not contain: `tsdown.config.ts` imports `../tsdown.client.ts`; `tsconfig.host.json` extends
`../../../tsconfig.base.json` with five project references; `tsconfig.client.json` extends
`../../../tsconfig.base.client.json` with nine.

dsh-run-speed README · Development：The declared dependencies are not the problem. `npm install` resolves every `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` pin from the public
registry in a couple of seconds — those releases carry the `next` dist-tag rather than `latest`, which is why
`npm view <pkg> version` suggests they are missing. What is missing here are the build tools themselves: the `test`
script needs `vitest` and the `bundle` script needs `tsdown`, and neither is declared in this `package.json` — they are
inherited from the monorepo root. In a bare clone, `npm test` therefore fails at the tool, not at the sources.

with in-repo equivalents — is the natural next step, and is not done here. The committed `lib/` artifacts are the build
output of `0.2.0-rc.2`; deliberate differences from the raw npm tarball — no build-machine paths, a shipped and

dsh-run-speed README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **Process-local selection** — the Host keeps the selection in a `WeakMap<Session, RunSpeedMode>` and it resets to
  Standard when DSH restarts. The control queries the Host for the authoritative mode whenever it mounts, and adopts
  the mode it just applied after a successful switch; it does not poll the Host afterwards, so it stays in step because
  both sides share the same command.
- **Policy rather than a throughput guarantee** — the plugin requests parallel work, but provider capacity, rate
  limits, task dependencies, and the model's own decomposition decision still determine wall-clock speed.
- **Status text is a wire contract** — the browser half parses the Host's `Run speed: <mode>.` reply to learn the
  current mode, so that wording is part of the Host/browser interface and must change in both places at once.

dsh-run-speed README · English summary：`dsh-run-speed` adds a per-session **Run speed** selector to DeepSeek Harness. It chooses how aggressively the
agent may fan work out to parallel background subagents — Standard (no added prompt text), Fast (up to 3), or Turbo
(4–6) — while explicitly preserving the selected provider, model, and reasoning effort. The selection is reachable from
the composer toolbar and from the `/run-speed` command, is stored in Host memory per session, and resets to Standard
when DSH restarts.
